processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sample was heated to 1200 °C at a rate of 10 °C/s (common pre-heat shared by all 24 conditions).
Homogenized by holding at 1200 °C for 120 s.
Cooled from 1200 °C to the set deformation temperature of 900 °C at 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at the set temperature (900 °C) before compression so the inside/outside temperature difference was eliminated.

Isothermal constant strain-rate compression on a Gleeble-3500 at 900 °C and 0.01 s^-1; mica foils with high-temperature lubricant were affixed to both end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool it down immediately.

structures.overall_structure: Initial (pre-deformation, as-forged) microstructure of the Fe-Mn-Al-C steel: large polygonal grains delimited by bright, continuous, slightly etched boundaries, with dark grain interiors; essentially every grain contains abundant fine, closely spaced parallel light striations whose direction changes from grain to grain, giving strongly banded dendritic/interdendritic segregation contrast (chemical heterogeneity) rather than a uniform solid solution. Grains are large relative to the 100 µm scale bar (individual grains span roughly one to a few times the bar length).

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: large polygonal grains, individual grains span roughly one to a few times the 100 µm scale bar

structures.overall_structure: After 60% isothermal hot compression at 900 °C / 0.01 s^-1 the sample underwent dynamic recrystallization (DRX). The DRX average grain size was measured from the core of the compressed sample (large deformation zone 3). At 900 °C the DRX average grain size of the alloy lies within roughly 8–13 µm for all four strain rates, with the lowest strain rate series (0.01 s^-1, i.e. this sample) being the coarsest of the four. Compression produces three deformation zones with differing recrystallization degree (zone 3 large deformation > zone 2 small deformation > zone 1 difficult deformation).

average_grain_size.value: ~8–13 µm (at 900 °C; figure-derived, 0.01 s^-1 series is the coarsest)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: dynamically recrystallized grains; grain size increases with decreasing strain rate and increasing temperature

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Isothermal constant strain-rate hot compression on Gleeble-3500; maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricant at both end faces to reduce friction/deformation non-uniformity; water-spray cooling after compression.

characterization_methods.technique: isothermal constant strain-rate hot compression (thermo-mechanical simulation)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 900 °C, 0.01 s^-1, maximum 60% compression (true strain 0.92); specimen Ø8 mm × 12 mm; mica foils with high-temperature lubricant at both end faces
characterization_methods.purpose: obtain the rheological (flow) stress curves and the DRX characteristic values of this 900 °C / 0.01 s^-1 condition
characterization_methods.key_findings: The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material; flow stress decreases with increasing temperature and decreasing strain rate. Peak stress at 900 °C / 0.01 s^-1 is 305.4 MPa.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: LEXT OLS4000 laser confocal microscope; etchant 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis, then prepared, ground, polished and etched; grain size measured in the core (large deformation zone)
characterization_methods.purpose: observe the microstructure of the deformation zones and measure the DRX average grain size
characterization_methods.key_findings: DRX average grain size increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; at 900 °C all four strain-rate series fall within roughly 8–13 µm.

computational_details.simulation_method: finite-element simulation coupled with regression of DRX average-grain-size data
computational_details.software_used: DEFORM-3D finite element software; Levenberg-Marquardt optimization algorithm for regression
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as a rigid-plastic body and die indenter as a rigid body; semi-symmetric specimen used as deformation model to shorten simulation time; billet-die contact-interface friction set to shear type with value 0.3; billet-air convection coefficient set as 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C); simulation in line with the experimental hot-compression conditions.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53% between predicted and experimental grain size; absolute error mostly within 3 µm.

analytical_models.equation_role: predicts the dynamic-recrystallization average grain size d_rex as a function of strain rate and temperature

computational_details.simulation_method: constitutive analysis (Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine equation + Zener-Hollomon parameter)

analytical_models.equation_role: relates peak stress, temperature and strain rate to determine the DRX activation energy of the steel

parameters.name: Qp (DRX activation energy, average over 900–1150 °C / 0.01–10 s^-1)

analytical_models.model_note: ε̇ = A[sinh(ασp)]^n·exp(-Qp/RT) (Eq. 1); Qp = 1000·R·k1·k2 (Eq. 2) with R = 8.314 J/(mol·K). Note: these are alloy-level constants fitted over all conditions, not unique to this sample.

analytical_models.equation_role: temperature-compensated strain rate parameter characterizing the combined effect of T and strain rate on flow stress
analytical_models.model_note: Z = ε̇·exp(Qp/RT) (Eq. 3); the lnZ value 64.08 is that tabulated for this sample's condition in Table 1.

unmapped_findings: For this sample (900 °C, 0.01 s^-1) the calculated Zener-Hollomon parameter is lnZ = 64.08 (Table 1), the highest lnZ of the 0.01 s^-1 row, reflecting the lowest deformation temperature of the experimental grid.
The steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material: increasing strain rate or decreasing temperature raises the flow stress (b0021, b0084).

The DRX activation energy of the steel (Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine fit averaged over the whole 900–1150 °C / 0.01–10 s^-1 range) is Qp = 669.844 kJ/mol (b0032, b0085); this is an alloy-level average, not unique to this sample.
The maximum compression true strain for all conditions, including this one, is 0.92 (60% reduction) (b0018).

Compression produces three distinct deformation zones in the specimen (1 difficult, 2 small, 3 large deformation); the degree of dynamic recrystallization ranks zone 3 > zone 2 > zone 1 (b0060, b0063, figure_008).

The DRX average grain size of the steel increases with decreasing strain rate or increasing temperature; at high T and low strain rate (e.g. 1150 °C, 0.01 s^-1) the grain size exceeds 70 µm and the structure becomes coarse (b0063).
